rationale: The book's core is carried directly by the definitional texts it prints (Deut 6:25 equating righteousness with observing/doing the commandments; Ps 119:172 identifying the commandments themselves as righteousness; 1 John 3:7 equating the one who does righteousness with the one who is righteous) plus the explicit identification in the proving chapter that the wedding garment/fine linen is the righteous acts (dikaiōmata) of the saints (Rev 19:8). These establish the active performance of the law as the referent more cleanly and with fewer mediating steps than the common forensic-status reading, which must relegate the same texts to secondary 'fruit/evidence' or 'standard' status. The multi-witness symbolic method and the already-accepted premises (love = keeping commandments; knowing = covenant relationship proven by obedience) further tighten the fit. Secondary claims that absolutely exclude any verdict/status sense, or that fully specify the garment's grant-wash-wear mechanics as indispensable to the identity, remain less secure against the full range of Pauline 'counted/apart-from-works' language and are therefore excluded from FULL support.
book_core_identification: Righteousness is the doing of God's commandments—the law kept as righteous acts performed.
book_secondary_elaborations: worn as the garment/fine linen of righteous acts (given, then arrayed by the wearer)
covenant covering that can be soiled and must be washed/kept
opposite of self-made fig-leaf coverings or nakedness/exposure
strongest_counter_interpretation: In mainstream Christian teaching (especially classic Protestant), righteousness primarily denotes the forensic/legal status of right standing before God—Christ's righteousness imputed/credited to the believer through faith alone—often pictured as a clean garment or robe that covers the sinner, with ethical doing of commandments as subsequent fruit, evidence, or outworking rather than the essence of the term.
counter_core_identification: Forensic/imputed status of right standing before God received through faith in Christ (not essentially one's own performance of the commandments).
material_core_denial: Denies that the essential referent of righteousness is the performance/doing of the commandments; treats that doing as secondary fruit or evidence of a prior declared status that is received independently of (or apart from) law-keeping.
counter_case: Genesis 15:6 / Romans 4:3-8: faith (of the one who 'worketh not') is counted/credited as righteousness, explicitly apart from works
Romans 3:21-26; 1:16-17: the righteousness of God is manifested/revealed apart from the law and received through faith in Christ
Philippians 3:9: Paul renounces 'mine own righteousness, which is of the law' for the righteousness that is through faith in Christ
2 Corinthians 5:21: believers become the righteousness of God in him (exchange language)
Isaiah 61:10 and related garment texts read as the covering of a received status rather than performed acts
Romans 3:20 / Galatians 2:16: by the works of the law no flesh is justified
book_explanatory_advantages: Takes the plain definitional syntax of Deut 6:25 ('it shall be our righteousness, if we observe to do all these commandments') and Ps 119:172 at face value without demotion to 'provisional' or 'standard only'
Matches the plural active dikaiōmata of Rev 19:8 exactly ('the fine linen is the righteous acts of the saints') rather than collapsing it into a singular status
1 John 3:7 becomes a direct identity statement rather than a mere evidential test
Consistent with the book's established multi-witness OT decoding method and with the prior accepted cores that love and knowing God are themselves constituted by commandment-keeping/obedience
Explains the wedding-garment exclusion (Matt 22) as absence of performed acts without requiring an extra layer of 'imputed covering later evidenced by acts'
counter_explanatory_advantages: Accounts for the repeated Pauline contrast between righteousness by faith and righteousness by works of law, including justification of the ungodly who 'worketh not'
Unifies the 'righteousness of God' phrases (Rom 1:17; 3:21-26) as God's own saving action/status gifted rather than human performance
Explains Abraham's justification (Gen 15:6) prior to the giving of the law and circumcision
Provides a ready reading of garment imagery as covering/imputation rather than woven acts
unresolved_objections: Precise coherence of 'faith counted for righteousness' / 'to him that worketh not' (Rom 4:5) with a core definition as commandment-doing requires additional distinctions (enabled doing, Christ as the doer, faith itself as first obedience, or rejection of 'own' self-generated works) that the proving chapter does not fully spell out
Whether every occurrence of 'righteousness of God' or 'become the righteousness of God' can be reduced to performed acts without remainder
The absolute exclusion of any verdict/status sense ('not a verdict only received') is stronger than the minimal core requires and remains contested by the broader Pauline corpus
